def: An object with dynamic storage duration initialized when an exception is thrown; its type determines which handlers can catch it. How it is stored is unspecified (global `operator new` is not called), and it is destroyed at the last potential point of destruction.

An exception from the completion of the initialization of the exception object until the completion of the activation of some handler for it; when rethrown it becomes uncaught again. `std::uncaught_exceptions()` returns their number.

The process, while control passes from the throw point to a handler, of destroying the automatic objects constructed since the try block was entered, in the reverse order of the completion of their construction.

A subobject that is not an anonymous union member and whose initialization is arranged by rules such as [[class.base.init]] and [[dcl.init.aggr]]; when the initialization of an object is terminated by an exception, such subobjects that have completed initialization are destroyed.

A handler from the completion of the initialization of the catch clause's parameter until the catch clause exits; when `std::terminate` is entered due to a throw, an implicit handler is considered active.
The exception whose handler was most recently activated and is still active; `throw;` rethrows it, and `std::current_exception()` returns it.

A predicate indicating whether a function can exit via an exception, given explicitly by `noexcept`/`noexcept(constant-expression)` or determined implicitly by rules; part of the function type since C++17.
The exception specification predicate is false, i.e. the function may exit via an exception. Ordinary functions without a *noexcept-specifier* are so by default.
The exception specification predicate is true. If the search for a handler leaves the body of such a function, `std::terminate` is called.

An expression that calls or implicitly calls a potentially-throwing function, a *throw-expression*, a `dynamic_cast` to a reference that requires a runtime check, a `typeid` applied to a dereferenced polymorphic pointer, or an expression with such an evaluated subexpression. The `noexcept` operator evaluates on this basis.
